run: Frequency and volume: you ran in all 4 weeks (vs 2 of 4 before and 3 of 4 last year). Total run distance is 39.5 km, +68% vs last year. Every run is capped at about 10 km.

Pace: average pace is 5:26/km, 34 s/km faster than last year and 25 s/km faster than the previous block. Without the 27 Sept run (4:42), the other three average about 5:40, still about 20 s/km quicker than last year.
Intensity: effort per hour is 138 vs 73 last year. Three of four runs scored 116 or more, so the Sunday run is a hard day every week.
Next steps: add a short easy run midweek and make most Sunday runs easy; try a 12–14 km long run every 2–3 weeks in a lower-cycling week.
ride: Volume: 315 km over 28 rides on 14 ride days, +25% vs last year with the same commute-style template.
Intensity is the weak spot: effort per ride is 24 vs 28 last year and no ride scored above 48.

Same loops, slower: the Antibes morning loop averages 33:27 vs 32:20 last year and the Valbonne evening loop 30:10 vs 29:04, both at lower effort. This fits fatigue from the added hard running but the data cannot prove the cause.
Next steps: after an easier week add one 40–60 km easy endurance ride and one structured threshold session.
overall: Where you stand: your biggest block of the three (+25% distance vs the previous 4 weeks, +28% vs last year), driven by consistency. The previous block is a lumpy baseline, so last year is the fairer yardstick.

Training load: 54% low aerobic, 46% high aerobic and almost no anaerobic load (6 points). Rides supply 90% of the low aerobic load, but also 47% of the high aerobic load: the Antibes morning climbs spend time in Z3–Z4, so the commute is not purely easy. The hard running adds the rest of the high aerobic load, and no session reached Z5 (178+ bpm).
Risk and plan: ACWR is 1.32 by effort and 1.57 by distance. Take an easier week next, then rebuild with one long easy ride, one structured ride and a Sunday run that is hard only every second week.
